title: 一体 — what on earth ～ (emphasizing a question)
summary: An adverb placed before a question word to show surprise, irritation or strong curiosity, as in 'what on earth' or 'who on earth.'

patterns.form: 一体＋疑問詞（何・誰・どう など）

body.p: It adds a strong feeling of 'I want to know' or 'I can't make sense of this' to a normal question. It appears with a question word: 一体何が起きたのか, 一体どうして.

Because it is emotionally strong, it may feel too pushy for polite questions to superiors. 一体全体 is even stronger. It also exists as a noun meaning 'the whole body,' but here it intensifies the question.

examples.ja: 一体（いったい）何（なに）が起（お）きたのですか。
examples.romaji: Ittai nani ga okita no desu ka.

examples.ja: こんな時間（じかん）に、一体（いったい）誰（だれ）が来（き）たのだろう。
examples.romaji: Konna jikan ni, ittai dare ga kita no darō.
examples.tr: Who on earth could have come at this hour?

examples.ja: あなたは一体（いったい）何（なに）が言（い）いたいのですか。
examples.romaji: Anata wa ittai nani ga iitai no desu ka.
examples.tr: What on earth are you trying to say?

pitfalls: It normally needs a question word. 一体行きますか is unnatural.
It carries strong emotion, so take care when speaking to superiors.
